hypothesis: Treating a harness-declared unsupported message stream as a capability boundary will stop false local-code repair tasks while preserving the control artifact and genuine coverage-gap routing.

metricsCompared.name: unsupported capability repair-task emissions
metricsCompared.baseline: one local-code pattern and one repair task from two recurring unsupported-stream fixtures
metricsCompared.candidate: zero actionable gap runs, patterns, or created tasks from the same two fixtures

metricsCompared.name: genuine control-gap routing regressions
metricsCompared.baseline: recurring external-payload-unscreened fixtures create one repair task
metricsCompared.candidate: recurring external-payload-unscreened fixtures still create one repair task

metricsCompared.name: focused control-coverage and dedupe tests
metricsCompared.baseline: unsupported harness capabilities were expected to become actionable health patterns
metricsCompared.candidate: 13 of 13 focused tests pass with the capability boundary non-actionable and genuine gaps unchanged

rationale: The candidate changes only health-review actionability. It retains operator-visible unsupported coverage in the canonical artifact, matches KOTA's existing trajectory-escalation treatment of declared unsupported capabilities, preserves evidence references, and passes focused positive and negative routing coverage plus type checking.
